anchors: ships no scripts, because clippy and criterion already do the mechanical part.
decision: The Rust skill is a checklist plus tool recipes and ships no scripts.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-06: Checklist + tool recipes (Recommended); clippy 0.1.95 perf group measured at 36 lints

reopen_if: A recurring Rust review step is done by hand that clippy and criterion cannot do.
why: clippy's perf group and criterion already do statically and by benchmark what the Python skill's scanners do by hand.

decision: A scripted pipeline like the Python skill's (setup, profile, scanners, prioritise).
reopen_if: Profilers are available on a test host and a repeated manual step appears.
why: Much of it would duplicate clippy, and with the profilers absent on the authoring host its parsers would ship untested against real output.

decision: A description opening 'Use when reviewing or improving the performance of Rust code', whose first fourteen keyword tokens include general words (reviewing, improving, code, loop, string, grown, without, capacity).

evidence.text: skill-router match() on nine prompts: the old head nominated this skill on 'review this Rust code for secrets handling and crate choices', 'review this Rust async code with tokio' and 'my Python loop is slow', and nothing on 'set up criterion benchmarks for my Rust parser', 'profile my rust binary with a flamegraph' and 'this async rust handler holds a lock across .await'; the new head reverses all six, 'my python script is slow, profile it' routes to coding-performance-review only, and 'fix the clippy warnings in this rust crate' to coding-rust only. Replay over 2478 distinct typed prompts from local transcripts: old head 8 nominations, 7 of them unrelated; new head 1, the Rust performance review request the old head also nominated.

reopen_if: The skill router stops deriving keywords from the head of the description, or MIN_HITS changes.
why: The router derives this skill's keywords from the first fourteen distinct description tokens and nominates on two hits, so 'rust' plus 'code' nominated it for Rust prompts about secrets, crate choices and async, and 'slow' plus 'loop' nominated it for a Python prompt, while criterion, flamegraph and .await-lock prompts got no match. A head of Rust and performance words (rust, slow, performance, benchmark, criterion, flamegraph, samply, perf, heaptrack, dhat, clones, with_capacity, spawn_blocking, await) fixes both.

decision: LazyLock needs Rust 1.80+, so check rust-version first and fall back to OnceLock (1.70+) or building once in the caller; a \d to [0-9] swap changes results on non-ASCII digits and needs a test.

evidence.text: LazyLock stabilised in Rust 1.80; regex crate \d is Unicode-aware unless (?-u). GREEN opus and haiku gave the caller-built fallback on rust-version 1.74 and no caveat in the 1.85 [a-z] control.

reopen_if: The skill's floor moves above Rust 1.80, or the regex crate's \d becomes ASCII by default.
why: A suggested rewrite used LazyLock and a regex swap with no toolchain check and no note on semantics, risking a compile break on an old toolchain or silently changed output.
